clue.text: Writer in dim novel about to happen (6)

definitions.note: IMPEND is a verb, 'to be about to happen'; the clue gives the phrase without 'be'

indicators.note: the writer goes inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters of DIM take a new order

blocks.note: DIM rearranged, split around the writer
a pen is a writer; it sits between IM and D

annotation.surface: An author appears in a dull novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' and 'novel' both push towards books, but a writer here is the tool, PEN, and 'novel' just means the letters change order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: a storm that impends is one set to arrive, the sense of hanging over what is coming.

blocks.note: at = in, as in 'at home'
a form is a class in a British school

annotation.surface: A pupil tells tales on classmates.
annotation.walkthrough: In British schools a class or year group is called a form. The question mark warns that 'at school' is not what it seems.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in slang: a snitch tells on others to those in authority, which is what informing on someone means.

clue.text: With pep, snorer turning a head (3,6)

indicators.note: the letters turn into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An energetic sleeper rolls over and moves their head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A head' looks like part of the sleeper's body; it is the price phrase, as in 'ten pounds a head'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'ten pounds a head' charges each individual ten pounds.

blocks.note: née, 'born', introduces a maiden name
d = died, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A life that began and ended in hardship.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a short sad biography; each word is a standard abbreviation from records of births and deaths.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being in want of money is poverty.

clue.text: Madagascar, perhaps, I left surrounded by beach? (6)

indicators.note: the L for left is enclosed by the beach word, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: as printed, first
l = left
beach = sand; L goes inside it, after the S

annotation.surface: A traveller leaves Madagascar, ringed by beaches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I left' reads as a traveller departing; I stays in front, and only the L is inside the beach. 'Perhaps' shows Madagascar is only an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': Madagascar is a land mass surrounded by the Indian Ocean.

indicators.note: the vessel goes inside the rearranged letters
the raids are a disaster, their letters wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: RAIDS rearranged
a pan is a cooking vessel; it goes after the S

annotation.surface: A European ship is caught up in disastrous attacks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship among raiders; it is a kitchen pan.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a native of Spain is one kind of European.

clue.text: Commander once more not at home (3)

indicators.note: the word for 'at home' is taken out

blocks.note: once more = again
at home = in; removed from AGAIN

annotation.surface: An officer has gone out again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Commander once' tempts as the definition with 'once' meaning former; 'once' belongs with 'more'.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical title: in the Ottoman Empire an aga was a military officer or chief.

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Britain
a pen for animals

annotation.surface: Strengthening the fence around land by a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border; it is the crossword's stock river.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the figurative sense: making a friendship or commitment stronger is making it run deeper.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the place name

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the name, after LINDIS

annotation.surface: Lindisfarne is a remote spot.
annotation.walkthrough: Lindisfarne is Holy Island, off the coast of Northumberland in north-east England, which makes the surface true.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe great distance.

clue.text: Forces plan a detour round the front (9)

indicators.note: the letters wanted are found round about the words before it, spread across them

blocks.note: the letters run from the last two of the first word to the first two of the last

annotation.surface: The military draws up a diversion around the front line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forces' and 'the front' paint a battlefield, so a solver hunts for army words; the answer is sitting in plain sight across forcES PLAN A DEtour.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense of 'front': the promenade along the seafront, which is what an esplanade is.

clue.text: Hit the mark with funny ending (9)

blocks.note: hit = punch
a line is a mark, as in 'toe the line'

annotation.surface: A boxer's blow lands, and the story ends in a laugh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit the mark' reads as one idiom, succeeding; split it into two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the last line of a joke, where the laugh lands.

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, and knocking it off removes it

blocks.note: a creek is an inlet; drop its C

annotation.surface: A foul odour from the water, strong enough to knock you out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smell' works as the noun or the verb, and the answer does both.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, noun or verb: a stench is a strong smell.

blocks.note: the plain meaning: a cure, as for a poison
lovesickness is doting; split the answer to see a word meaning 'against doting'

annotation.surface: A cure for the pangs of love.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer into ANTI and DOTE: something against doting, so a cure for being lovesick. The question mark flags that pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a pun inside: the word for a remedy, split, says it works against doting.

blocks.note: beyond = over
ta is British slang for thanks
ken = knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

annotation.surface: Someone passed away, owing it all to learning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passed beyond' sounds like dying, and 'thanks to' like 'because of'; both phrases break apart. Ken is an old Scottish word for knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the road: a car that has been driven past has been passed.

indicators.note: the letters are blown apart and land in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A faulty firework goes off after all, which is awful.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that a dud flare by definition doesn't explode; here its letters do.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are intensifiers for something very bad, from weather to acting.

indicators.note: the cleaner is put inside the swell

blocks.note: a surge is a swell of water
a char is a cleaning lady; it goes after SUR

annotation.surface: A smart cleaner slips in an extra charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as the adjective, great; it is the noun, a rise of the sea. A char (charwoman) is British for a cleaner.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an additional charge on a bill, such as a fuel levy, is extra money.

indicators.note: to regulate is to put in order, here a new one

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: An engine's choke controls itself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Choke' looks like the valve on an engine that regulates air; here it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to smother or suffocate, whether a person, a yawn or a protest.

clue.text: Prime time for making dried grass, so it's said (6)

indicators.note: what is said is heard, so the answer is how the phrase is pronounced

blocks.note: a day for haymaking, a hay day

annotation.surface: Summer is the best season for making hay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime time' reads as one phrase about television; only 'Prime' is the definition, and 'time' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a person's peak years, their time of greatest success.

clue.text: Tania included New Zealand with a country in Africa (8)

indicators.note: Tania takes the other letters inside her

blocks.note: as printed, split TA...NIA
NZ, the standard abbreviation for New Zealand
as printed, after NZ

annotation.surface: Tania's travels took in New Zealand and an African country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With a' tempts as a link, but the A is part of the insertion, NZ plus A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the East African state on Lake Victoria, home of Kilimanjaro.

clue.text: Dirty place at end of avenue is an eyesore (4)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: a pigsty, or any filthy place
last letter of avenuE

annotation.surface: A grubby spot at the end of the street spoils the view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' means an ugly sight; read literally, it is a sore on the eye.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of a figurative word: the painful swelling on an eyelid is truly a sore of the eye.

blocks.note: OTT = over the top
love = nil = O in tennis

annotation.surface: Someone has an obsessive passion for a film-maker.
annotation.walkthrough: Preminger was an Austrian-American film director; the surface turns his name into an object of adoration.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by name: the Austrian-American film-maker behind Laura and Anatomy of a Murder.

clue.text: File stuff away when superlatively soft (9)

indicators.note: the letters are sent off out of their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An office worker files the softest things away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'File stuff away' reads as office work; 'away' signals the letters of FILE STUFF are out of place.
annotation.definitionFit: A superlative for a superlative: the most downy, and so the softest.

clue.text: Pleasant times for power in America (3)

indicators.note: P goes inside the letters for America

blocks.note: p = power, as in physics
US = America

annotation.surface: Good times for those in power in America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pleasant times for power' reads as a politician's good spell; 'for' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain plural noun from the idiom 'ups and downs', where the ups are the good spells.

blocks.note: verb: to joke with someone, pull their leg
the animal's young, as a calf is a cow's

annotation.surface: Someone teases a baby goat.
annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses: a verb for joking, and the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the verb for teasing someone playfully, and the name for a goat's young.

blocks.note: not people standing but furniture: frames that hold something up
not a formal sitting room but a room where artists draw

annotation.surface: Guests standing about in a formal parlour.
annotation.walkthrough: A drawing room is a formal sitting room, and 'stands' looks like a verb; read it as a noun, and the room as one for drawing.
annotation.definitionFit: The stands are artists' supports for a canvas, which belong in a room used for drawing.

clue.text: Add up at end of day in Cumbria, perhaps (6)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: to count is to add up
last letter of daY

annotation.surface: Doing the day's sums in the Lake District.
annotation.walkthrough: Cumbria, home of the Lake District, is in north-west England; 'perhaps' shows it is just one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': Cumbria is an administrative region of north-west England.
